chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Abdul Salam ibn Nuaym, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I entered the House (the Kaaba) and nothing of supplication was present to me except the Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, no one has departed with anything superior to what you departed with.'

key_terms.الْبَيْتُ: The House (referring to the Kaaba in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of reciting Salawat upon the Prophet and his Household when entering the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the supreme merit of Salawat in Shia tradition, where Imam al-Sadiq (as) validates that even a spontaneous, unmemorized invocation of blessings upon the Prophet and his Household is sufficient for spiritual success. It underscores the concept that the essence of devotion lies in the sincerity of connecting with the Ahl al-Bayt, rather than the complexity of the supplication. This narrative reinforces the theological centrality of the Prophet's household as the primary means of intercession and divine grace.
